1.content: Give any move that strictly reduces the Manhattan distance to the goal a strong positive bias. Give any move that strictly increases the Manhattan distance a very large negative bias, but this penalty is subordinate to safety considerations: moves that would place the agent on a hazard cell or adjacent to a hazard retain a maximal (or strong) negative bias as defined in the Safety Heuristics, overriding the distance‑increase penalty. Such distance‑increasing moves are considered only when no safe distance‑decreasing moves exist.

2.content: Assign a maximal negative bias to any move that would place the agent on a hazard cell, overriding all other bonuses (including distance‑reduction). For moves that would place the agent adjacent (including diagonally) to a hazard, apply a strong negative bias that dominates progress bonuses unless no safe distance‑decreasing moves exist; in that case, allow a moderate penalty so the move can be considered.
